B596.what_changed: sample of 12/12/6 replaced by the FULL 2,176-set 13-stone layer, and the G_11 path lengths that round2/round3 recorded as NOT-COMPUTED are now exact
B596.method: BFS from the 16 maximum sets of n=7 over the 1-stone-move graph restricted to the size window [floorK, 14]. Neighbours are filtered by conflicts_a so every emitted node is a safe set; the BFS is therefore exact and complete inside the window.

independent_cross_check.note: the C++ BFS reproduced round2's Python census exactly

B598.what_changed: the ratio's numerator was shown to be ambiguous: 'layer size' vs 'true neighbourhood of the maximum configurations' give completely different growth
B598.new_stage: extend -- counts t(S) = #{M in M_n : S subset of M} for every (K_n-1) set

double_counting_check.verdict: the multiplicity distribution is exhaustive and exact

B598.interpretation: read literally as 'the number of NEIGHBOURS of a maximum configuration', the ratio is 1.5, 2, 5.9, 8.3, 10.4, 14 -- roughly linear in n, far below n^2. The B597-favouring reading is therefore strengthened, but the asymptote is still undecidable because n=8 is not enumerable.

B599.verdict: PARTIAL -> PARTIAL (certificate constructed; the 'few carriers' part is refuted)
B599.what_changed: the constructive certificate requested in round2/round3 was actually built and verified against the full 16-set maximum pool
B599.definition: cl(T) = smallest SAFE superset of T = fixpoint of 'if a forbidden quad has 3 points in the set, the 4th is forced'. A forbidden quad is exactly 4 points on one line or one circle, so cl(T) > K_n proves 'no maximum set contains T' by pure circle/line capacity.

cert2.note: for every t, the sets excluded by the closure and the sets absent from the maximum pool agree on all 1716 seven-subsets; the closure never certifies a false positive at t=4 (27+395=422 of 715, the remaining 293 are in neither category)

B599.what_is_refuted: round2's note suggested '3-4 circles could force |S^M| <= 5'. The actual certificate needs 32 carriers (30 circles + 2 lines) for a 4-point blocking subset -- about 10x the suggested figure.

B591.new_content: quantified the break in the trend: adjacent differences of the max d_max sequence 2,3,4,8,6 (n=4..8) are +1,+1,+4,-2; n=7 is the unique local maximum of both the absolute and the relative quantity
B591.necessary_constant: C >= 8, forced by n=7; n=8 does not strengthen it
B591.unchanged: the existence of an absolute constant C is an infinite-family statement and is not decidable by any finite layer

B592.new_content: the saturation closure of the n=7 worst set shows d_max=8 arises from a 7-point forced block (any 7-subset saturates the whole 49-point board), i.e. a saturation bisection. The same shape appears at n=6 (d_max=4 with a 10-stone layer), suggesting d_max ~ |S|/2, which would make d_max/n ~ 1/2 and would be enough for B592's 'some c>0'
B592.unchanged: d_max/n maxima 1/2, 3/5, 2/3, 8/7, 3/4 for n=4..8; the 14-stone layer of n=8 is not enumerable

B593.new_content: the same saturation mechanism accounts for both c=1 and c=2 at n=7 (d_max=8 for both), so the qualitative claim 'the repair cost scales with the deficit' is mechanistically confirmed at n=7
B593.unchanged: the n-independence of C is undecidable; the c=1 ratio sequence 2,3,4,8,6 (n=4..8) does not rule out growth
